issues.body: The module docs and always-compiled `VerifiedCredentials` docs link to `VerifiedCredentials::admit_data_integrity`, but that method exists only under `cfg(feature = "acp-vc")`. With the feature off (the default and an explicitly required supported state), rustdoc cannot resolve these intra-doc links. Similar unconditional links appear in `lib.rs`. This is the feature-gated intra-doc-link failure class called out by the repository's gates.
issues.fix_hint: Make feature-neutral prose use code formatting rather than an intra-doc link, or gate the linked paragraphs/doc attributes with `cfg(feature = "acp-vc")`. Check both default-feature-off docs and `--all-features` docs after updating every unconditional link to the gated method/type.
issues.title: Feature-off rustdoc links target a nonexistent method

issues.body: `credential_subject` returns the first triple with the `credentialSubject` predicate anywhere in the signed graph. It neither anchors that predicate to a specific credential node nor rejects multiple distinct subjects. RDFC verification canonicalizes the graph, so the same valid signed triples can be presented in a different slice order and cause a different subject to be selected and credited. On an authorization boundary, ambiguous subject binding must fail closed rather than depend on caller-controlled input order. The current tests cover one subject only and do not expose this.
issues.fix_hint: Define and enforce an unambiguous credential root/subject model (for example, require exactly one distinct credentialSubject for the admitted credential and reject zero or multiple subjects), then add a test with two distinct credentialSubject triples that presents the same signed graph in both orders and confirms deterministic rejection rather than granting either agent.
issues.title: Credential subject binding is ambiguous and presentation-order dependent

verdict.summary: The fail-closed ACP rule path and its end-to-end tests are substantive, but the new always-compiled public API contains intra-doc links to an item that does not exist when the default-off `acp-vc` feature is disabled. That violates the required feature-off documentation/build state. The verifier also selects the first credentialSubject predicate anywhere in the signed triple set, without identifying the credential node or rejecting ambiguity; because RDFC signatures are order-independent, callers can reorder a valid multi-subject presentation and change which agent receives the holding. Both issues should be fixed before approval.
